# `extension-changed`

Unclassified x- extension changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `docs` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `extension-changed` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Docs (annotations only) ([RULES.md section 10](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An `x-` extension the policy does not classify as `wire` or `sdk` changed.

## Why this default

Treated as documentation unless the policy says otherwise.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  extension-changed: info
```

## How to fix

Classify extensions that affect clients or SDKs in the policy `extensions` section.
